subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu direct session can become unusable after /reset or /new and fall back to generic 'Something went wrong...' while session index points to missing transcript IDs

question: Should all direct-chat `/new` and `/reset` rotations be required to create the target transcript before publishing the new session id, or should some paths remap back to the last valid transcript instead?
rationale: Both outcomes are plausible recovery contracts, and the existing labels already indicate maintainer/product review before changing reset semantics across reply, runner, and gateway paths.

options.title: Require transactional rotation
options.body: Every reset/new path creates or verifies the target transcript header before committing the new id and lineage, and failures keep or remap to the prior valid transcript.

options.title: Add repair-only recovery
options.body: Leave runtime rotation mostly as-is but add doctor or startup repair that detects missing transcript family members and remaps them to the newest valid transcript.

options.title: Fold into broader Feishu UX work
options.body: Defer the durability fix until the broader Feishu failure-translation issue owns reset recovery and user-facing fallback copy together.

recommendation.title: Require transactional rotation
recommendation.body: Every reset/new path creates or verifies the target transcript header before committing the new id and lineage, and failures keep or remap to the prior valid transcript.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has the strongest recent history on reply session initialization and session lifecycle seams where the contract choice would land.
